alignments.note: Imperative `עָדָה` with the reflexive *thyself* its own sense licenses (rule 44) and the *with* by which the English verb reaches its bare Hebrew object `גָּאוֹן` — no object marker and no preposition of its own stands on that noun, which is rule 44's condition and its `טָחוּ תָּפֵל` → *have daubed ... with untempered mortar* precedent. Discontinuous around *now* under rule 25; the head stays on the lexical verb.
`נָא` rendered by the single word *now* rather than by the full entreaty formula; rule 30 directs aligning only what the ASV writes.

Bare direct object of `עָדָה` (accusative of material). The supplied *with* is licensed by the English verb's valency and stays with the verb under rule 44, so this noun keeps only its own word; rule 33's adverbial-accusative reading, which would put *with* here, is the competing analysis and is rejected because the noun is the verb's object rather than an adjunct.
Waw opening the second line, rendered *And* (rule 14).

`הוֹד` rendered *honor*; the ASV reorders the pair, and each waw is placed by the numerals-and-connectives count of rule 42 — this waw stands before `הוֹד` and the English *And* stands before its clause.
Waw standing between `הוֹד` and `הָדָר`, taking the *and* the ASV writes between *honor* and *majesty* (rule 14).

`לָבֵשׁ` recast as *array thyself*, with the reflexive its own sense licenses and the *with* by which the English verb reaches its bare Hebrew objects `הוֹד` and `הָדָר` (rule 44). Head on the lexical verb.

review_notes: Corrected: the accepted alignment gave the first supplied *with* to the object noun under rule 33 and the second to its verb under rule 44, though both Hebrew nouns are bare direct objects (accusative of material) of their verbs, with no object marker and no preposition of their own. Rule 44's own limit says to read which the Hebrew noun is before placing the word, and treating two identical constructions in one verse by two different rules is not an allocation clearly preferable to the alternatives under rule 2. Both *with*s now go to their verbs on rule 44's `טָחוּ תָּפֵל` → *have daubed ... with untempered mortar* precedent.

The competing reading, giving both *with*s to the nouns under rule 33, remains statable; it is rejected because rule 33 governs an adverbial adjunct and these nouns are the verbs' objects. JOB.40.22's `צִלֲלוֹ` is the contrasting case in this chapter: there the verb already has its object in the suffix, so the supplied *with* is rule 33's.
The verb units are discontinuous around *now* and around the reflexive pronoun under rule 25; the reflexives stay with their verbs because the verbs' own sense licenses them (rule 44).
